subject: ss-haematology
title: Sickle cell disease vaso occlusion and organ care
refs: Harrison Principles of Internal Medicine 22e Ch 103 Disorders of Hemoglobin
American Society of Hematology guidelines for sickle cell disease 2020

steps.tx: **Sickle cell disease** (SCD, sickling haemoglobin disorder) follows a single **glutamate to valine** substitution in **HBB** (beta gene), forming **HbS** (sickle haemoglobin). **HbSS** (homozygous disease) is the severest form and **HbSC** is milder. **HbF** (fetal haemoglobin) inhibits sickling and naturally modifies severity. **Polymerisation** (fibre formation) deforms cells, stiffening them and triggering **vaso occlusion** (vessel blockage pain).
steps.say: A single valine substitution in the beta gene forms sickle haemoglobin. Polymer fibres deform red cells and block small vessels. Fetal haemoglobin naturally protects against sickling.

steps.tx: Triggers are predictable: **hypoxia** (low oxygen), cold, dehydration, infection, acidosis and altitude. **Dactylitis** (painful hand foot syndrome) is the infant hallmark, while older children suffer **stroke** (brain vessel occlusion) and adults endure **sickle bone pain** (vaso occlusive crisis). **Acute chest syndrome** (lung sickling complication) follows infection, surgery, asthma or abrupt haemoglobin fall and demands oxygen and transfusion.
steps.say: Cold, dehydration, infection and hypoxia trigger sickling crises. Dactylitis is the infant hallmark, while stroke strikes older children. Acute chest syndrome follows infection or surgery and demands urgent care.

steps.tx: Chronic haemolysis and autosplenectomy reshape childhood. **Splenomegaly** early gives way to **autoinfarction** (spleen self destruction) by age **5**, leaving functional **asplenia** and twin infection risks from encapsulated organisms. **Penicillin prophylaxis** (preventive antibiotic) starts from **2** months in many programmes, and pneumococcal vaccination is mandatory. **Parkland** habits of fever, pain and chest symptoms always raise sickle emergencies.
steps.say: The spleen infarcts by age five, leaving functional asplenia. Encapsulated organisms thrive without splenic filtration. Penicillin prophylaxis and pneumococcal vaccination protect young children.

steps.tx: **Hydroxyurea** (HbF inducer, ribonucleotide reductase blocker) cuts pain crises by **44** percent and acute chest events substantially, and it is offered early in children and adults. Starting at **15** to **20** milligrams per kilogram daily and titrating by **MCV** (mean size) and counts earns steady benefit. **Voxelotor** (haemoglobin oxygen modulator, withdrawn in 2024) and **crizanlizumab** (P selectin blocker, withdrawn after failure) mark changing options. **NSAIDs** (pain relievers) plus opioids manage crises.
steps.say: Hydroxyurea cuts pain crises by nearly half and is offered early. Voxelotor was withdrawn in twenty twenty four over safety signals. Crizanlizumab also failed confirmatory testing.

steps.tx: Transfusion saves lives in stroke and acute chest, with **simple transfusion** (top up) for stable patients and **exchange transfusion** (automated red cell swap) preferred in stroke to cut HbS below **30** percent fast. Chronic programmes need phenotype matching to prevent **alloimmunisation** (antibody formation). **Chelation** handles transfusional iron after about **20** units. Screening for alloantibodies precedes every chronic programme.
steps.say: Exchange transfusion is preferred in stroke to cut HbS below thirty percent quickly. Simple top up suits stable patients. Phenotype matching prevents alloimmunisation in chronic programmes.

steps.tx: **Stroke** (brain infarction) prevention uses annual **transcranial Doppler** (TCD, brain blood flow scan) from age **2**, with abnormal velocities under **200** centimetres per second defining risk. Chronic exchange transfusion protects high risk children. **HSCT** (stem cell transplantation) cures disease with matched donors, and **gene therapy** (lentiviral beta addition) plus **CRISPR** (fetal haemoglobin reactivation) are now approved. **Pulmonary hypertension** (lung pressure rise) screening with echo guides referral.
steps.say: Annual transcranial Doppler screening runs from age two. Chronic exchange transfusion protects high risk children. Stem cell transplantation cures disease with matched donors.

steps.tx: Organs fail slowly. **Nephropathy** (kidney disease) begins with albuminuria, while **retinopathy** (eye vessel change) threatens vision in HbSC. **Avascular necrosis** (bone blood loss) strikes femoral and humeral heads, and **priapism** (prolonged erection) emergencies need oxygen, fluids and exchange rather than waiting. **Pregnancy** amplifies crisis, chest and clot risks, so combined haematology obstetric care is essential. Screening urines and fundi yearly is standard.
steps.say: Kidney disease starts with albuminuria, while retinopathy threatens vision in HbSC disease. Bone infarcts strike hip and shoulder heads. Priapism needs oxygen, fluids and exchange promptly.

steps.tx: **Global health** lessons matter. Newborn screening enables penicillin before first sepsis, and **PVOC** (pneumococcal vaccine) plus Hib vaccines are lifelong. In India, **HbS beta thalassaemia** and HbS beta plus compound heterozygotes complicate interpretation, and **GWAS** (genome wide studies) identify HbF modifiers. **Opdivo** confusion aside, **lactate dehydrogenase** and reticulocytes track haemolysis, while cold drinks and **meperidine** (pain drug) worsen sickling. Patient education is itself treatment.
steps.say: Newborn screening enables penicillin before the first sepsis. Vaccines and patient education are themselves treatment. Mepiridine worsens sickling and cold drinks trigger crises.

steps.tx: Follow through pays. **Pain management** follows a ladder from NSAIDs to opioids with oxygen, fluids and incentive spirometry for chest prevention. **Anticoagulation** helps only selected acute chest subsets, not routine pain. **Deferasirox** chelates chronic transfusion iron. **HSCT** donor search starts early, since matched siblings are rare. Quality of life scores improve most with fewer crises, not merely higher haemoglobin.
steps.say: Pain follows a stepped ladder with hydration and spirometry support. Anticoagulation helps only selected chest subsets. Donor search for transplantation starts early.

steps.tx: Exam anchors: single valine substitution gives HbS; **HbSS** is severest; autosplenectomy by age **5**; hydroxyurea at **15** to **20** milligrams per kilogram cuts crises by **44** percent; TCD from age **2** screens stroke; exchange transfusion is preferred in stroke; **voxelotor** withdrawn in 2024; and **CRISPR** reactivation therapy is approved. Meperidine and cold drinks are classic sickling triggers students must name.
steps.say: A single valine substitution creates sickle haemoglobin. Hydroxyurea cuts crises by nearly half. Stroke needs exchange transfusion, not simple top up.
